items.title: Unique purely inseparable p-power extensions of one-variable function fields over a perfect field

author_roles.attribution_basis: Official solution PDF header; course-document attribution, not an individually identified writer.

items.source_title: ETH Algebraic Geometry II, Autumn 2017 — official Solutions 14
items.difficulty_reason: For a finitely generated transcendence-degree-one field extension of a perfect characteristic-p base, the author minimizes [K:k(t)] to force t^(1/p) outside K, compares finite field degrees through Frobenius-induced isomorphisms and tower multiplicativity, and identifies K^(1/p)=K(t^(1/p)); the opening induction extends uniqueness to degree p^r. The generator choice and degree-comparison construction are carried by this proof rather than supplied as a conclusion.
items.statement_scope: Sheet14 Q1(a) only, including its common setup: k is a perfect field of characteristic p>0, K/k is finitely generated of transcendence degree1, and r>=1. The only purely inseparable extension of K of degree p^r is the overfield {x^(1/p^r): x in K}. No genus or curve assertion from Q1(b) is counted.

statement_spans.label: Q1 common opening Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p>0, followed by part(a) in full through the overfield {x^(1/p^r):x in K}; stop before printed part(b). The common setup is part of this standalone statement.

proof_spans.label: Q1 Solution:(a) begins By induction on r the problem reduces to the case r=1 on p1. Retain both field-tower/Frobenius diagrams across pp1-2. End at L=K(t^(1/p)), as desired on p2, immediately before proof(b).

source_caveats: Original pages1-2 retain the printed statement/proof of Q1(b) and the beginning of Q2; only Q1(a) and its common field setup are counted.

Official solution PDF header names Prof.Richard Pink; author fields express official course-document attribution. Coordinator Alexandre Puttick is not inferred to be the writer; individual_solution_writer remains null.
Q1(b) is held because the course standing context for curves/genus has not been located. Its HOLD is not a classification as H1 and does not alter the self-contained field hypotheses of Q1(a).
The original author induction and degree/Frobenius diagrams are retained. No generated TeX, added proof, substituted p-basis proof or strengthened hypothesis is introduced.

Frobenius isomorphisms over a perfect base
